criterion: The records it parses are limited to the repository it was asked about, and the answer is unchanged for every case the existing tests cover
summary: Stated in the order it happened, because the first version of this claim was false. previous_bypass reads journal.read_repo(repo) instead of journal.read(), and the in-loop repo skip is gone because every record it consulted already had to pass it. Submitted as equivalent, that was wrong: a differential comparison against the pre-change implementation over 400 generated journals found 3 disagreements. The cause was in the WRITER, not the reader - `repo` sat in journal.SHEDDABLE_FIELDS under a comment saying identity fields are never shed, so a record could be written past its own repo. Every reader ignored such a record, but _cut_position matches on the fields that are never shed and so still found it; narrowing the read hid it from one half of the function and not the other. `repo` is no longer sheddable, and after that change the same comparison reports 0 disagreements over 400 journals. An independent reviewer built its own rig and reported 15 disagreements in 400 journals with the old shed list restored and 1 in 5000 with the current code. Equivalence therefore holds from commit 31a7c74 onward, not from a6c8edd, and not for repo-shed records already on disk: the writer changed, so an old one stays as invisible as it was.
